correctness.rationale: Reconstructing from the two Stern pair digit maps (a,b)→(a,a+b) and (a+b,b) gives adjacent coprimality and the two flanking values a+k(a+b), b+k(a+b) for n+1=2^k(2u+1); this works also at k=0 and at n=0. Their difference and coprimality give gcd(2k+1,a−b). Reznick's Theorem 4.7 concerns arbitrary initial intervals and each fixed modulus d≥2, including composite moduli; d=1 is trivial. Primitive diagonal pairs modulo p^a number p^a−p^(a−1) of p^(2a)−p^(2a−2), so CRT yields the claimed q_d. The allowed run lengths start at (d−1)/2 and have step d; their geometric weights give the stated closed factor. The proportion with k≥K is at most 2^(−K) in every interval [0,N), by counting multiples of 2^K in [1,N]. This permits both conditioning and tightness; exact value h on each fixed k is a finite congruence condition. For inversion one may first use finite divisor inversion within each run stratum and then sum over strata: the absolute majorant ∑(2k+1)2^(−k−1) is finite. The stratum k=(h−1)/2 contributes strictly positive mass for each odd h. Independent bit-map replay confirms the identity on 65,536 indices and exact rational evaluations at d=3,5,7; an independent conditional mixture agrees with the Möbius series, which yields 0.89734042214605 with absolute truncation error at most 2^−49.
residual_risks: No uniform rate in the modulus or independent reproof of the modular equidistribution theorem; the finite replay is only arithmetic corroboration.
